title: Claim: fixtures-are-dependency-injection-for-tests
body: Fixtures inject dependencies into tests; this makes setup explicit and tests more readable.

title: Claim: conftest-py-shares-fixtures-across-tests
body: Fixtures in conftest.py are automatically discovered and available to all tests in that directory and subdirectories.

title: Claim: fixture-scope-balances-reuse-and-isolation
body: Function scope ensures isolation; module or session scope reuses setup. Choose the right scope for your trade-off.

title: Claim: fixtures-compose-building-complex-environments
body: One fixture can depend on another; Pytest resolves the chain and runs setup in order.

title: Claim: yield-in-fixtures-simplifies-cleanup
body: Using `yield` in a fixture separates setup and cleanup; code after yield runs after the test.

title: Complexity: simple fixture (no dependencies, function scope)
body:
**O(1) setup, O(1) cleanup per test**

minimal overhead

title: Complexity: session-scoped fixture (reused across all tests)
body:
**O(1) setup once; O(1) cleanup at end**

expensive setup amortized across all tests

title: Complexity: fixture composition (fixture depends on another fixture)
body:
**O(1) per dependency; resolved in order**

dependency resolution is linear in dependency depth

title: Complexity: fixture with monkeypatch (patching module globals)
body:
**O(1) patch, O(1) restore**

restores patches automatically after test

title: Complexity: parameterized fixture (@pytest.fixture(params=[...]))
body:
**O(n) where n is number of parameter values**

test runs once per parameter value

title: Q1: What is dependency injection in pytest?
body:
A. Tests directly instantiate objects and pass them to fixtures
B. Tests declare parameters matching fixture names; pytest injects the fixtures
C. Tests import fixtures explicitly from a fixtures module
D. Tests call a setup function before each test

**B.** Pytest uses the test function's parameter names to match fixtures. If a test has a parameter named 'tmp_path', Pytest injects the built-in tmp_path fixture.

title: Q2: What is conftest.py?
body:
A. A configuration file for pytest settings
B. A pytest file that defines shared fixtures available to all tests in that directory and subdirectories
C. A test file that runs configuration checks
D. A file that imports all test modules

**B.** conftest.py is a pytest convention; fixtures defined there are automatically discovered and available to all tests in that directory and subdirectories.

title: Q3: How does the `yield` keyword in a fixture work?
body:
A. It skips the test if the condition is false
B. It returns a value from the fixture
C. It separates setup (before yield) from cleanup (after yield)
D. It makes the fixture run in parallel

**C.** yield separates setup and cleanup in a fixture. Code before yield runs before the test; code after yield runs after the test, even if the test fails.

title: Q4: What does fixture scope control?
body:
A. Whether the fixture is visible in other test files
B. When setup runs and when cleanup happens (function, module, session)
C. How many tests can use the fixture
D. The order in which tests run

**B.** Fixture scope determines: function-scoped fixtures run before each test; module-scoped fixtures run once per module; session-scoped fixtures run once per session.

title: Q5: How can a fixture depend on another fixture?
body:
A. By importing it explicitly
B. By calling it directly
C. By declaring the other fixture as a parameter
D. By registering it in conftest.py

**C.** A fixture can take another fixture as a parameter. Pytest resolves the dependency chain and runs setup in order.

title: 1. Multiple tests need the same temporary directory
body:
**Pattern**: test declares tmp_path parameter; pytest injects it

**Why**: Avoids manual tempdir cleanup; pytest manages it. Each test gets a fresh directory.

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture (tmp_path is built-in)`

title: 2. Setup and cleanup must be coordinated (e.g., start/stop a server)
body:
**Pattern**: setup before yield; cleanup after yield

**Why**: Cleanup is guaranteed even if the test fails; no manual try/finally needed.

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture with yield`

title: 3. A fixture depends on another fixture (composition)
body:
**Pattern**: fixture_a takes fixture_b as parameter

**Why**: Avoids duplication; complex environments built from simple fixtures.

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture, parameter passing`

title: 4. Expensive setup (database) should be reused across tests
body:
**Pattern**: @pytest.fixture(scope='session' or 'module')

**Why**: Amortizes expensive setup cost; tests run faster.

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture(scope=...)`

title: 5. Run the same test with 10 different inputs
body:
**Pattern**: @pytest.fixture(params=[...]) or @pytest.mark.parametrize(...)

**Why**: DRY: avoid copy-pasting the test 10 times.

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture(params=...) or @pytest.mark.parametrize(...)`

title: Signal: Multiple tests need the same resource (database, temporary d
body:
**Structure**: fixture with @pytest.fixture decorator, injected as test parameter

**Requirement**: DRY: avoid duplicating setup logic in each test

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture, yield for cleanup`

**Example**: all tests need a temporary directory; define tmp_path fixture once

title: Signal: Setup and cleanup must happen in a specific order
body:
**Structure**: fixture with `yield` to separate setup and cleanup

**Requirement**: Automatic teardown without explicit cleanup code

**Python**: `def fixture(...): setup_code; yield; cleanup_code`

**Example**: start a server, yield, then stop it

title: Signal: A test depends on multiple resources (database, mock, config
body:
**Structure**: fixture takes other fixtures as parameters

**Requirement**: Compose fixtures; avoid deeply nested setup

**Python**: `def fixture_a(fixture_b, fixture_c): ...`

**Example**: a service fixture depends on a database fixture and a config fixture

title: Signal: Expensive setup should be reused across tests (avoid repeati
body:
**Structure**: session or module-scoped fixture

**Requirement**: Balance speed (reuse) and isolation (fresh state)

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture(scope='module' or 'session')`

**Example**: database connection or service startup, reused across tests

title: Signal: Run the same test with different parameter values
body:
**Structure**: @pytest.fixture(params=[...]) or @pytest.mark.parametrize

**Requirement**: DRY: avoid copy-pasting the test

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture(params=...) or @pytest.mark.parametrize(...)`

**Example**: test the same function with 5 different input values
